notes: Dates as printed: Original Effective Date 12/31/00; Reviewed 08/27/26; Revised 09/15/26. effective_date holds the original effective date, reviewed_date the review date; the revision date is recorded here.

The guideline 'applies to all lines of business unless otherwise noted in the Program Exceptions section'. Program Exceptions: FEP follows FEP guidelines (excluded from NIA review); State Account Organization follows SAO guidelines; Medicare Advantage products follow NCD 240.4.1 (Sleep Testing for OSA), NCD 240.4 (CPAP), LCD L38398 (HGNS), LCD L33405 (Polysomnography and Sleep Testing) and Article A57496.
Preauthorization may be required under certain contracts, and site-of-service criteria based on comparative effectiveness studies are applied during preauthorization; neither is a chart criterion.

'Determining the Appropriate Site of Service' (evaluation of signs/symptoms with history and physical, comorbid conditions, secondary sleep disorders, and cognitive/physical ability to test at home) describes the ordering provider's selection process rather than a requirement a chart must document for coverage; it is left out of the trees. Its substance is carried by the HSAT pathway's conditions B and C and the PSG/split-night comorbidity and sleep-disorder branches.

The Note under 'Diagnostic Testing' (ordered by a licensed physician or advanced practice provider; reviewed and interpreted by a board certified sleep physician) is a general requirement placed in every pathway's 'all' as two answerable:false criteria (provider credentials are not shown by a chart).

The comorbid medical condition list and the secondary/concomitant sleep disorder list are printed six times with minor wording differences (HSAT B, PSG B/D, titration C, split night B/D, repeat titration B/C). Each item is one criterion whose text is taken from one printing (split-night B for comorbidities, which reads 'chronic use of oxygen' and 'immunomodulator biologics' where the HSAT printing has 'chronic use oxygen' / 'immunomudulator/biologics'; the titration printing for central sleep apnea, which omits the 'Previously diagnosed' that the HSAT and PSG printings carry). The HSAT printing of the opioid item says 'on most days for greater than 3 months'; the others say 'on most days per week'. The titration-C printing of the opioid item is truncated in the PDF ('for greater').

Where the PDF breaks a line at a hyphen (light-headedness, treatment-emergent, Prader-Willi) the extracted text joins the halves, so criterion texts stop short of those words: the arrhythmia criterion ends at 'supported by clinical documentation' (the parenthetical examples are in the question) and the pediatric neurologic-disorder criterion is 'neurologic disorder' (examples Down syndrome, Prader-Willi syndrome, myelomeningocele in the question). Two statements are interleaved with their table-row headings in the extracted text, so their texts are the first contiguous clause: 'pediatric members younger than age 18' and 'Diagnostic testing (CPT codes 95808, 95810 and 95811) for CDL'.

Every comorbidity and sleep-disorder list is introduced with 'such as', i.e. an open list; the trees use the listed items only. For HSAT condition B ('Absence of ... such as') the tree is not(any(listed items)).

Comorbidity items that define one condition by alternatives (heart failure: NYHA III/IV or EF <= 40%; COPD/ILD on PFTs or chronic oxygen use; OHS: pCO2 > 45 and pO2 < 60) are kept as single criteria; a threshold is attached only where one number defines the item (pulmonary artery pressure > 40 mm Hg, opioid use > 3 months, PLMD >= 15 per hour).

Attended PSG: the document says '(A&B, A&C, or D)', so condition D (secondary/concomitant sleep disorder) stands alone without A; the split night study says '(A&B or A&C or A&D)' and the tree follows each literally.

PSG condition C and split-night C ('Recent HSAT (less than 1 year old) confirmed to be non-diagnostic') are built as all(HSAT less than 1 year old, any(technically inadequate AND valid retest attempt, failed to establish OSA in a member with high pretest probability)). 'Of note: there is no minimum required HSAT recording time for HSAT to be considered diagnostic' is explanatory and not a criterion.

Full night attended titration: the Note says attended titration is for 'members (age 6 and older)' and requires a prior diagnostic study confirming significant OSA plus the member not being appropriate for unattended APAP titration. Age 6 and older is included as a criterion; 'confirmed significant OSA' is condition A; 'not appropriate for APAP' is expressed by conditions B, C and D. APAP (E0601) coverage is noted on the pathway, not built (E0601 is not in the coding section).

Titration A.2 is printed with a typo ('greater than or greater than or equal to 5 events per hour but less than 15'); the criterion text keeps the typo so it is verbatim; threshold gte 5 with the upper bound (< 15) left to the question.

Titration D (APAP failure) bullets 1 and 2 each hold two requirements (residual AHI >= 5 / residual EDS, and adequate objective adherence) and are split; the adherence text is one shared criterion. Bullet 3 is any(not a candidate for auto bi-level, auto bi-level tried and not effective). Bullet 4 is all(unable to tolerate PAP after a 1-month minimum APAP trial, not(previous attended titration)); the bracket in the PDF is unclosed.

Repeat diagnostic testing: the document says the member must 'meet criteria for a HSAT, PSG or split night as outlined above' and ONE of conditions 1-4. Built as three pathways (repeat HSAT, repeat PSG, repeat split night) so that a repeat test of a given type must meet that type's own initial criteria; each embeds the initial tree. Condition 4 (oral appliance) is offered as 4a (efficacy assessed using HSAT) on the HSAT pathway and 4b (manual adjustment during PSG) on the PSG pathway; the Note says 95811 is not correct coding for oral appliance adjustment, so it is not offered on the split-night pathway. The 4b sub-bullets ('may request in-facility polysomnography (95810) ... if meets current criteria for an in lab evaluation' and 'Alternatively, the oral appliance may be adjusted in the office empirically and then HSAT may be performed') are permissive elaborations covered by the pathway structure and are not separate criteria.

Repeat diagnostic testing condition 3 is built as all(reassessment after surgical intervention, any(listed surgeries)). Condition 2's second bullet holds two requirements (persistent or recurring signs or symptoms of OSA; adherent with PAP therapy) and is split.

'If previous diagnostic test or baseline study is not available, physician attestation will be accepted and sleep study type will be determined by medical necessity' (repeat diagnostic testing) has no explicit requirement in that section to waive, so it is recorded here. The second attestation sentence concerns replacement PAP therapy or supplies, which this guideline does not cover. 'Sleep studies performed outside the United States are accepted as long as the sleep report contains sufficient data to determine medical necessity for the diagnosis' is an acceptance rule, not a criterion.

Repeat attended titration: '(1 and 2 or 3)' is read with 'and' binding tighter: any(all(1, 2), 3), i.e. a previous titration insufficient to determine the correct pressure justifies a repeat on its own. A reader could instead read all(1, any(2, 3)). The NOTE that physician attestation is accepted when the previous diagnostic test is not available is an 'any' at condition 1's 'diagnostic sleep test has been submitted'. 'a member who is known to have OSA' is a criterion of the pathway.

Repeat titration condition 1 bullet 1 holds two requirements (recurrence of OSA related symptoms; adherent to PAP therapy) and is split; its adherence wording differs from the APAP-download adherence wording in the full-night titration section, so they are separate criteria.

MSLT: read literally, 'previous evaluation has not demonstrated a diagnosis of OSA' cannot coexist with the fourth bullet (member on PAP for OSA with resolution on download). Built as all(persistent excessive daytime sleepiness, any(all(no OSA on previous evaluation, any(ESS >= 10, unintentional naps > 3 months, symptoms suggestive of narcolepsy)), all(on PAP for OSA, adherent, download demonstrates resolution)), follows a facility-based PSG or in-lab titration, not(after a split night study)). The fourth bullet's 'has persistent daytime sleepiness' is the shared top-level criterion. The Note's 'always follows a facility-based PSG (95810) or an in lab titration (95811)' and 'should not be performed after a split night study' are treated as requirements a chart can show.

MSLT 'Epworth Sleepiness Scale greater than or equal to 10' reuses the signs/symptoms ESS criterion (same requirement). 'for at least more than 3 months' is given threshold gte 3 months. 'Recurrent symptoms suggestive of narcolepsy' is one criterion; the examples (cataplexy, sleep paralysis, hypnagogic hallucinations) are 'not limited to' and are named in the question.

Actigraphy: 'one-time covered service' is a frequency limit and is recorded on the pathway, not as a criterion; the chart criteria are 'in lieu of sleep logs to evaluate sufficient sleep and assess sleep-wake schedules' and 'prior to MSLT testing'.

CDL / government license testing: the statement is an exclusion with a waiver ('unless the member meets criteria for in facility testing or home testing'); it is recorded as an exclusion and adds no pathway, since such a request is judged by the ordinary pathways.

Pediatric: the sign/symptom gate ('is evaluated when there is the presence of one or more of': snoring; labored, paradoxical or obstructed breathing; sleepiness, hyperactivity, behavioral or learning problems) is attached to the first PSG indication ('Obstructive sleep apnea is suspected based on clinical signs/symptoms') rather than to every indication, since indications such as unexplained cor pulmonale, primary apnea of infancy or evaluation prior to decannulation do not depend on those symptoms. A reader could instead require the symptom gate for all pediatric PSG indications.

Pediatric PSG 'Following adenotonsillectomy in a child with ANY of the following' is printed with every later indication at the same bullet level. The tree keeps under it only the post-adenotonsillectomy items (mild preoperative OSA with residual symptoms; preoperative evidence of moderate to severe OSA, obesity, craniofacial anomalies or neurologic disorder; under 3 years old; cardiac complications of OSA; failure to thrive) and treats the items from 'Suspected congenital central alveolar hypoventilation syndrome' onward as stand-alone indications, because they cannot sensibly depend on a prior adenotonsillectomy. This is a judgment call a reader could make differently.
Pediatric split night (95811) is its own pathway with the pediatric PSG tree, per the NOTE that the member must meet criteria for pediatric in-facility polysomnography.

Pediatric titration: the Note 'PAP titration may also be undertaken in a child with other sleep-related breathing disorders (not obstructive sleep apnea) when treatment with NIPPV is recommended' is built as a fourth alternative branch (all(other sleep-related breathing disorder, NIPPV recommended)) beside A&B, A&C and A&D. Condition B ('Follow-up for child on chronic PAP support ... due to growth and development; if symptoms recur while on PAP') is one criterion covering both reasons. 'Snoring' in A.2 reuses the pediatric sign/symptom criterion. 'pediatric members younger than age 18 years' is a criterion of every pediatric pathway.

Hypoglossal nerve stimulation: the heading says 'Attended sleep study (polysomnography (PSG) or Home Sleep Apnea Test (HSAT)', so the pre-implant pathway governs both PSG and HSAT codes. Criterion 5 is built as any(CPAP failure, all(CPAP intolerance, shared decision making that the patient was intolerant of CPAP)) because the shared-decision clause concerns intolerance; a reader could attach it to both. 'AHI is 15 to 65' carries threshold gte 15 with the upper bound (65) in the question. Post-implantation testing is two pathways: PSG for device titration, and subsequent HSAT/PSG retesting for insufficient response or weight gain with return of symptoms.

Exclusions list each non-coverage statement with cpt [] unless the code itself is non-covered; only 95807 is marked non-covered in the coding table. Indication-level exclusions (insomnia, circadian rhythm disorders, RLS, screening, snoring only, employer-required testing, etc.) and use-level exclusions (HSAT to monitor PAP efficacy, HSAT in children, oximetry, < 3 channel devices, PAP-Nap) are kept in the exclusions list rather than as not-leaves in the pathways, since the document states them outside the criteria. The HSAT-section list and the Noncovered-section list overlap; both are recorded. The reference list identifies PAP-NAP as CPT 95807-52, but the exclusion bullet names no code.

The cephalographic x-ray exclusion carries a carve-out: lateral cephalographic x-rays and orthopantograms may be medically necessary for evaluating members for oral appliances, and lateral cephalographic x-rays to evaluate members for obstructive sleep apnea surgery; neither has a code in this guideline.

The adult attended PSG, split night and HSAT-related pathways carry no age criterion other than HSAT's 'Age 18 years or older'; the Description calls PSG the standard test 'in adult patients', while 95808 is 'any age' and members younger than 18 are governed by the pediatric pathways (95782, 95783, 95808, 95810, 95811).

Codes: the coding section lists 95782, 95783, 95800, 95801, 95803, 95805, 95806, 95807 (Non-covered), 95808, 95810, 95811, G0398, G0399, G0400. E0601 (APAP) appears only in the position statement and is omitted; the supply codes A4556-A7044 in the Reimbursement section are included in the sleep test allowance, not separately covered, and are omitted. No ICD-10 codes are listed.

Reimbursement limits (not chart criteria): sleep testing (95782, 95783, 95800, 95801, 95806, 95808, 95810, 95811, G0398, G0399, G0400) limited to two in 12 months; MSLT (95805) limited to one day of testing in 12 months; one repeat 95805 may be covered if the first test was invalid or uninterpretable in a member with a high clinical pretest probability of a sleep disorder, or the member has more than one sleep disorder; 95805 is allowed in addition to 95808, 95810 or 95811; the overnight stay and listed supplies are included in the sleep test allowance. Services in excess are subject to medical review of documentation (history and physical, procedure note, treatment plan, EEG and PSG study).

The Description section's statements (PSG monitored for 6 or more hours; HSAT for adult members 18 or older; AASM recommendations) are background, not criteria; HSAT's age requirement is in the position statement as condition D.

Thresholds not attached: neck circumference (two sex-specific numbers), the oxygen desaturation items (a saturation and a percentage of recording time each), central sleep apnea (> 50% central and >= 5 per hour), OHS (two blood gas values), CPAP intolerance (hours per night and nights per week).
Second check (FABLE_KEY_CRITIQUE.md): criterion no_previous_attended_titration now has positive text to match its question under the not; the id is kept.
